_readme: One real-car photo per chip colour, picked by eye from freely-licensed Wikimedia Commons photos (searched, downloaded, visually checked against the measured chip swatch). 'confidence' is my own visual judgement, not a pixel measurement: good = clearly the right colour family and plausible shade; tentative = right family but the shade, lighting or a repaint makes it uncertain; none = no credible real-car photo found despite searching. Colours with no DB/RAL-grade real photo are left for the user to judge from the chip + reference image alone.

db1600.note: No real curry-yellow 406/416 photo found (curry yellow was dropped in 1991 and seems rare in surviving photos).

db1624.note: No real amber-yellow photo found distinct from the chrome-yellow / yellow-orange ones below; those may actually be this colour instead.

db2550.note: Bright yellow-orange flatbed, Netherlands. Clean daylight shot, straight-on body panels.
db2550.author: Alf van Beem

db2603.note: Museum-plaque 406 in Slovenia, deeper/redder orange than the NL truck above — but under a wooden shelter, warm ambient light, so the shade may be skewed.
db2603.author: Shabicht

db6277.note: Pale sage green, close-up of the open driver's door — right family, but no wide shot to confirm overall tone, and it's a worn original finish so could have faded.
db6277.author: GoMinU Unimog

ral6014.note: Olive-khaki 406, daylight, clean side view — good match for the measured chip.
ral6014.author: order_242 from Chile

db6821.note: FLAG: saftgrün (sap green) should read as a yellow-olive green by its name, but this truck is a vivid teal — which actually matches our scan-skewed chip measurement (#39A17E) suspiciously well. Either the chip scan is more correct than assumed, or this truck was repainted a non-factory teal. Worth a second look either way.
db6821.author: Norbert Schnitzler from Aachen, Deutschland, NRW

db7187.note: No confident lorry-grey match; the two grey/beige candidates found (cabrio, 416 agricole) read closer to grey-white and pebble grey respectively.

ral1004.note: Bright gold-yellow 6x6 with a crane, Amsterdam. Good saturated match for a bright yellow — but could equally be amber yellow DB1624; no second yellow photo to separate them.
ral1004.author: Bart

db1474.note: No real desert-sand photo found; see db7701 for the closest grey/beige candidate, assigned there instead.

db2553.note: No real photo distinct from fire red found; red-orange and fire red are close in hue and the one clear red photo found reads as pure red (assigned to db3534).

db3534.note: Bright red 406 pickup at a show, UK. Clean daylight, good match.
db3534.author: Steve Glover from Bolton, Lancs., England

db5361.note: Deep glossy blue 406 pickup, Weelde oldtimer show. Good match; see also 1976_unimog_406.jpg (a brighter blue, in sources/photos/ already) as a second real-car reference.
db5361.commons: File:2009 08 22 Weelde 142240 - Beautiful blue vintage Unimog 406 pickup truck.jpg
db5361.author: Norbert Schnitzler

db6294.note: Dark teal-green convertible with tarpaulin, parked next to a similar dark green truck. Plausible for the near-black RAL 6005 moss green, but the exact shade is hard to judge from the photo's shade/lighting.
db6294.commons: File:Green Unimog 406 convertible with stake bodies and tarpaulin.jpg
db6294.author: GoMinU Unimog

db6840.note: Bright minty green 406 at a classic car show — lower confidence: this reads more like a saturated kelly/mint green than the yellow-green (hellgelbgrün) the chip measures, could be a repaint or show polish.
db6840.commons: File:1979 green Mercedes-Benz Unimog 406 at Techno Classica 2013 in Essen, Germany.jpg
db6840.author: GoMinU Unimog

db7701.note: Pale warm grey-beige 416 agricultural model, parked in a village street — plausible for kieselgrau (RAL 7032 is itself a beige-grey), but overcast/mixed lighting makes the exact tone uncertain.
db7701.author: Didier Bastia

db9136.note: Very pale grey/near-white 406 cabrio with red wheels, outdoor overcast light — could be grey-white or a primer finish rather than a factory topcoat; flagged for a second look.
db9136.author: Nanzig
